The product behavior is correct, and memory-level coverage exists (test_memory.py:141). The gap is this end-to-end check, which prints PASS for an allergy property it never examined.
findings.reproduction: Ran `acceptance.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8795 --no-restart` against the scripted preview: `PASS  recommendations still avoid peanut ... 13/13 checks passed`. scratch/audit/accept_probe.py shows that turn's data: `mentioned: [] -> picks: [] -> peanut_free(r) = True`, and that a mutant profile `{'remembered': ['Allergies: peanut'], 'this_conversation': ['Allergies: none (saved: peanut)']}` gives `has_allergy(mutant) = True`.
findings.fix: Before 'yes', send 'What do you recommend?' and require non-empty, peanut-free picks. Also check that no this_conversation line starts with 'Allergies:'.

findings.title: documented app-written behaviors have no test: six mutants survive
findings.evidence: Mutants were applied one at a time to a scratch copy of the project; test_app.py stayed at 79 passed for each. (a) _changes_line's 'Just this conversation:' became 'Every visit:'. That line is the README's fix for a live failure and README tour step 5. (b) The reply model was called with extract_model; FakeLLM ignores model and output_config. (c) The notice was removed from the briefing. (d) Budget was shown as '$15' instead of 'up to $15.00'. (e) History was no longer trimmed to HISTORY_MESSAGES. (f) The idle purge in start_conversation was removed.

Have FakeLLM record model= and assert that it equals reply_model on reply calls.

merged.title: A long-running preview server keeps every reply-model briefing in memory

findings.title: The conversation scorer (check, summarize) has no tests
findings.evidence: grep shows nothing imports eval_conversations. check() produces the README's headline 'unsafe recommendations' and '42/42, 75/75'.
findings.reproduction: grep -n eval_conversations *.py video/*.py -> only its own docstring lines
findings.fix: Add test_eval cases that run run_case with FakeLLM: an ineligible pick produces an UNSAFE line, a missed expectation is counted, and an extraction failure is not correct.

findings.title: A turn where extraction failed counts as fully correct
findings.evidence: check() checks only the expectations, and the unchanged state satisfies several of them: question-saves-nothing, tonight-only turn 3, past-diet turn 2, and the 'not sure' turn. The app's reply there is 'I couldn't process your dietary preferences...'. extraction_failures is reported separately, but cases_correct and turns_correct include these turns, and the README Evidence table omits extraction failures.
findings.reproduction: run_case(question-saves-nothing) with FakeLLM returning invalid JSON -> reply 'I couldn't process your dietary preferences right now...'; summary `{'cases_correct': 1, 'cases': 1, 'turns_correct': 1, 'turns': 1, 'extraction_failures': 1, 'unsafe_recommendations': 0}`

findings.title: The diet branches of restriction recall and spurious restrictions, and the latency quantiles, are untested
findings.evidence: Diet accounts for 3 of the 10 active and 3 of the 8 durable recall units. No test predicts a missed or spurious diet, and _latency is tested only with constant values.

findings.fix: Add three tests: predict nothing for 'I'm vegetarian now.' and assert a missed diet unit in each layer; predict vegan for veg-01 and assert a spurious diet; give _latency [1,2,3,10] and assert p50/p95.

findings.title: Invalid model output counts as an exact-claim match and a decision match on noop cases
findings.evidence: On error, claims=[] and p=simulate(profile, []). `"exact": Counter(map(_norm, expected)) == Counter(map(_norm, claims))` is True when expected_claims==[], and decision_match is True whenever the labels produce no change. In the app a failed extraction does not behave like a noop: it replies _EXTRACT_FAILED.
findings.reproduction: .venv/bin/python -c "evaluate_extractor(cases, lambda u: ([], 'ValueError: bad'))" -> `invalid 1.0 exact 0.062 decision 0.219`; exact&invalid: ['noop-29-third-party','noop-30-question']; decision_match&invalid: veg-05, veg-08, alg-19, spice-23, noop-28, noop-29, noop-30. The published run had invalid_output_rate 0.0, so its numbers are unaffected.
findings.fix: In score_case, set exact = decision_match = False when error is not None, and add a noop case to test_invalid_output_counts_as_invalid_and_as_missed.

findings.title: Classifier failures score as correct 'unclear' answers, and the false-yes headline cannot detect an outage
findings.evidence: classify_reply_with_stats turns any MODEL_ERRORS/ValueError/KeyError/TypeError into 'unclear' and returns no error flag. evaluate_confirmations then counts it as correct for the 6 cases labelled unclear, and false_yes is 0 by construction. The rows have no error field. eval_conversations inherits the same behaviour: the 'Hmm, I'm honestly not sure.' turn passes on a failed call.
findings.reproduction: evaluate_confirmations with a client that always raises anthropic.APIConnectionError -> `{'cases': 18, 'accuracy': 0.333, 'false_yes': 0, 'confusion': {'yes->unclear': 6, 'no->unclear': 6, 'unclear->unclear': 6}}`. Every row of the published run has output_tokens >= 11, so the published 18/18 is genuine.
findings.fix: Record the error in stats (e.g. stats['error']) from classify_reply_with_stats, add a 'failed' count to the confirmations summary, and exclude failed rows from accuracy.

findings.title: A saved soft scalar (budget, spice, lean) can't be cleared unless the customer repeats its exact value
findings.evidence: The R5 negation needs the held value ('if not any(v[attr] == claim.value ...): NOOP'), and _check_value(required=True) rejects a missing value. The extractor sees only the message, not the profile. So 'forget my budget' either fails validation, which rejects the whole message (other claims in it, an allergy included, are dropped and the customer is asked to rephrase), or carries a guessed number, which becomes a no-op.
findings.reproduction: parse_claims with budget_max negate value=None plus an allergen claim gives 'SpecError: budget_max needs a value' (the whole message is rejected). Held 15, negate value=20 gives 'R5 noop negated value is not currently held -> budget still 15'
findings.fix: Allow value=None on a negation of a soft scalar and treat it as 'clear whatever is held' (REMOVE at claim scope). Keep the value requirement for diet (§5.2).
findings.note: File is read-only (chmod 444) by the owner's choice; any fix is the owner's decision.

findings.title: Liking and disliking the same ingredient both stay saved; the ticket and the reasons contradict each other
findings.evidence: R6 'return Decision(events=(draft(op, scope, value),), rule="R6", ...)' writes only (disliked_ingredient, X). (liked_ingredient, X) is a separate canonical key and is never retracted. The extractor prompt covers only the reverse direction ('no longer minds ... negates disliked').
findings.reproduction: snippet: liked mushroom, then disliked mushroom, then recommend(load_menu(), active). Output: 'liked {mushroom} disliked {mushroom}', 'S5 -3.5 (has mushroom, which you dislike, has mushroom, which you like)', 'M7 -3.5 (...same...)'
findings.fix: In decide R6, when asserting liked_ingredient or disliked_ingredient X, also emit a REMOVE of the opposite attribute's X at the same scope.
findings.note: File is read-only (chmod 444) by the owner's choice; any fix is the owner's decision.

findings.title: A durable proposal whose only effect is on the active overlay is always rejected as stale when the customer says yes
findings.evidence: decide judges a durable claim against both views ('views = ... (durable, active)', §5.1), but resolve judges it against one: 'target = now.durable if d.scope is Scope.DURABLE else now.active; if _hard_effect(...) == "none": raise StaleConfirmation'. With a tonight-only sesame overlay, 'I'm not allergic to sesame' gets R10 with a DURABLE REMOVE. Durable has no sesame, so every yes raises. The customer is asked a question no answer can satisfy, and then told 'The earlier question no longer applies'.
findings.reproduction: snippet: conv SET sesame, then negate sesame (current), then answer(yes). Output: 'R10 confirm Scope.DURABLE "Should I stop treating sesame as an allergy? ..."' / 'StaleConfirmation: the proposed change no longer changes anything' / 'active allergen after yes: {sesame}'. Diet: overlay vegan plus hedged omnivore gives 'Should I save omnivore as your diet going forward?', then StaleConfirmation, and active stays vegan
findings.fix: Judge freshness in resolve the way decide judged the claim: effect = _combine(_hard_effect(..., v) for v in ((now.durable, now.active) if d.scope is DURABLE else (now.active,))). Or have decide propose at Scope.CONVERSATION when the durable effect is 'none'. Pair this with the companion fix above.
findings.note: File is read-only (chmod 444) by the owner's choice; any fix is the owner's decision.

findings.title: Two proposals from one message: both questions are returned and shown, but 'yes' answers only the last
findings.evidence: Conversation.handle: 'if d.proposal is not None: # one at a time: a new question replaces the old one / self.pending = Pending(...)'. The earlier Decision keeps its proposal and question in the returned list, and agent.turn shows every dec.question. 'I'm not allergic to peanuts or sesame anymore' (or 'nuts', which the README says becomes peanut + tree_nut) asks two questions. The customer's 'yes' removes only the second, and the first is dropped without notice. This fails safe (the allergy is kept) but contradicts what was asked.
findings.reproduction: MENUMIND_NO_APP=1 snippet with Agent + FakeLLM: turn 1 saves peanut and sesame; turn 2 negates both. Reply: '**Should I stop treating peanut as an allergy? ...** **Should I stop treating sesame as an allergy? ...**'. Turn 3 'yes' gives 'Every visit: no longer avoiding sesame.' and 'saved allergens: [peanut]'
findings.fix: Hold proposals in a FIFO and ask the next one after each answer. Minimal alternative: at the end of handle, replace earlier decisions whose proposal is not self.pending with proposal=None, question=None, so only answerable questions are shown.
findings.note: File is read-only (chmod 444) by the owner's choice; any fix is the owner's decision.

findings.title: Liked and disliked ingredients don't match ingredients inside house recipes
findings.evidence: has_ingredient checks only top-level names: 'any(word == ing or word in ing.split("_") for ing in self.ingredients)'. The loader judges allergens and diet through _parts(), but taste matching doesn't. 'I hate garlic' penalizes only S2, though 6 dishes contain garlic. agent.menu_words likewise builds its vocabulary from top-level names only.
findings.reproduction: recommend with disliked={w}. garlic: contains [M1,M10,M2,M4,S2,S5], penalized [S2]. soybean: contains 7, penalized []. sugar: contains 7, penalized [D3]
findings.fix: Match over parts as well: any(word == p or word in p.split('_') for ing in self.ingredients for p in (ing, *_parts(ing))).

findings.title: The 'typed price' and dish-name checks are easy to bypass
findings.evidence: TYPED_PRICE = r'\$\s?\d', and names use plain 'item.name.lower() in lowered'. The module docstring says check_reply rejects 'any full dish name or price typed in the message', and the README says prices always come from the menu. A wrong price in words, or a name with a double space, hyphen or NBSP, passes.
findings.reproduction: check_reply returns [] for '[[item:M5]] is just 12 dollars tonight.' (real price $16), 'costs USD 12.', 'is $.99 off.', 'Shrimp  Pad Thai', 'Shrimp Pad-Thai', 'Shrimp\xa0Pad Thai'. Only '$12.' is flagged
findings.fix: Widen the price pattern (\d+(\.\d+)?\s*(dollars?|usd|bucks)|usd\s*\d|\$\s*[\d.]). Normalize text and names (NFKC, collapse whitespace and hyphens) before the substring test.

findings.title: If the conversation can't be started after sign-in, the error goes to the hidden sign-in form and the app shows a blank chat with no conversation
findings.evidence: In the auth submit, `showApp(); await startConversation(false);` and then `catch (err) { $("auth-error").textContent = err.message; }`. #auth-error is inside #auth, which showApp() just hid. conversationId stays null. On page load, `catch { showAuth(); }` likewise turns any /api/me or startConversation failure (500, network) into an unexplained sign-in form.
findings.reproduction: Playwright scratch/audit/ui_checks.py scenario B: POST /api/conversations returns 500 once, then a new account registers. Output: `app visible: True | auth visible: False` / `auth-error text (hidden section): 'Something went wrong.' | log text: ''` / `conversationId: None` / sending a message then shows `problem shown after sending: '[object Object]'`.
findings.fix: In the auth handler, show a startConversation failure where it is visible: add("problem", esc(err.message)) after showApp(), or call showAuth() before setting #auth-error. In the load IIFE, call showAuth() only for err.status === 401 and show other errors.

findings.title: Sign out ignores a failed logout request: it shows the sign-in screen while the session stays valid
findings.evidence: `await api("/api/logout", { method: "POST" }).catch(() => {}); me = null; showAuth();`. The session cookie is httponly, so only the server can end it. If the request fails, the user is told nothing and remains signed in. On a shared device, a reload reopens their account and saved allergies.
findings.reproduction: Playwright scratch/audit/ui_checks.py scenario C: /api/logout aborted, then reload. Output: `after Sign out: auth visible: True | any error shown: ''` / `after reload: app visible: True | Signed in as ui300a82`.
findings.fix: Call showAuth() only after logout succeeds; on failure, add("problem", ...) saying sign-out failed and keep the app shown.

findings.title: No test runs the chat page's JavaScript; the confirmed UI defects (stale reply, hidden errors, failed sign-out) are untested

The /api/chat fields the page reads (changes, trace.claims[].polarity etc., question) are not contract-checked over HTTP either.

findings.title: test_http_trace_keeps_internal_errors_out cannot detect leaks of reply_errors/rejected (raw model output and SDK error text)
findings.evidence: The test sends 'Something is wrong with me.', an extraction failure whose trace holds only claims and extract_error. reply_errors and rejected never exist on that turn, so the filter for them is never exercised.

On a normal turn the mutant exposes them: `mutant trace keys on a normal turn: ['claims', 'decisions', 'fallback', 'rejected', 'reply_errors']`.

findings.title: eval_conversations.py, the scorer behind the README's safety headline, has no test
findings.evidence: test_eval.py tests eval_extractor's scorer against an oracle and targeted mistakes. eval_conversations.check() and summarize() have no test: check() decides 'UNSAFE' (hard_violations against profile.active) and summarize() computes unsafe_recommendations and cases/turns correct (README: '0 in 75 turns', '42/42, 75/75'). For example, checking profile.durable instead of profile.active, or skipping kind=='rec' filtering, would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Confirmation-lifecycle gaps hid three of the defects above
findings.evidence: No property test checks that every proposal decide() raises can be affirmed right away (that would catch the overlay-stale bug). No test resolves a Scope.CONVERSATION proposal or checks question wording by scope. No test covers two proposals in one handle() call. No test covers a companion overlay followed by the customer's own removal. No test covers EventStore.append rollback of a partly failed batch (I verified that it does roll back).
findings.reproduction: A pytest plugin wrapping memory.decide (scratch rulecov.py) over all non-sweep tests saw no proposal with scope conversation being answered. The repros above pass with the suite at 75/75
findings.fix: Add: (1) for each sweep base, affirm each proposal and assert no StaleConfirmation; (2) a two-proposal message; (3) companion plus own removal; (4) append rollback with evidence=None in the second draft.

findings.title: The original's inline TRACE is stale and partly not producible by MenuMind, but is labelled 'recorded output'

Or [[rec:S4]], it's a favorite.', …]; menu M3 allergens NEW ['sesame','soy'] ORIG ['gluten','sesame','soy']; tests '196 passed in 1.63s' vs '136 passed in 1.99s'. findings.title: the Whisper read-back gate passes one-word misreads (it passed 'Sauté' for 'satay') and never checks numbers
findings.evidence: 'misread = [... if r < 0.9]'. _words() (line 78-81) drops NUMBER_WORDS and every digit (regex [a-z]+), so numbers are never compared, although the heard() docstring says they are. With SequenceMatcher, one substituted word in an n-word section scores (n-1)/n, which is >= 0.9 for n >= 10, and the shortest sections have 14 words. Docstring line 9: 'a misread line stops the build'.
findings.reproduction: _words('a hundred and ninety-six tests') == _words('a hundred and ninety-five tests') == ['a','and','tests'], ratio 1.0. The cached transcript vo/S05-3f940f88_n.heard.txt reads 'Sauté and pad thai are never suggested.' and scores 0.955, so it passes; the gate did not catch the misread that SAY now patches. Also passing: S06 'pad tie' (0.929), S18 'rule of mind' (0.967), and S17 with 'Validation:' dropped (0.965).
findings.fix: Fail on any word-level replace/insert/delete opcode that is not in a small per-word allow-list of known Whisper spellings. Map digits in the transcript to words (or compare against the script's numbers) instead of discarding numbers on both sides.

findings.title: Per-beat checks do not cover several things the narration and mark labels say
findings.evidence: The docstring promises 'Each beat checks that the app did what the narration will say'. Gaps: (1) remove_yes has no check on the picks, yet S10 says 'her picks still follow what she saved' with mark 'Recommended from what she saved' (this is the brief's 'personalized recommendations based on remembered preferences'); (2) allergy has no check that satay and pad thai are shown flagged, yet the S05 label says 'Flagged by the app, never recommended'; (3) the question check is only `'not suitable for you' in r['reply']`, not that the warning is beside the pad thai; (4) after 'No, just for tonight.' the S07 reply_first label 'Kept for tonight only' sits on unchecked model text.
findings.reproduction: Code reading, plus the current frames viewed: 000251 (satay and both pad thais flagged), 000446 (model: 'only for tonight'), 000738 (picks follow hot spice). The current take happens to satisfy all four, but a take that didn't would not be retaken.
findings.fix: Add shoot.check calls: remove_yes `picks(r)` non-empty and none containing mushroom; allergy `{'Chicken Satay','Shrimp Pad Thai','Tofu Pad Thai'}` each followed by 'not suitable' in the reply; question 'Pad Thai** ($' followed by 'not suitable'; hedged reply mentions 'tonight'.

findings.title: The previous good footage is deleted before a new take succeeds, and non-Retake errors abort without a retake
findings.evidence: `shutil.rmtree(RAW)` runs at the start of every attempt, but beats.json and capture_data.json are written only on success. After 3 Retakes, or any Playwright TimeoutError (expect_response 120 s, wait_for_function 30 s), KeyError and so on, which `except Retake` does not catch, RAW holds a partial failed take while capture_data.json is still the old one. The good take is gone, and build.py then fails with no beats.json.
findings.reproduction: reasoning: lines 311-332; only Retake is caught, and the rmtree happens before serve()
findings.fix: Film into RAW.with_name('raw.new'), swap it in on success, and treat playwright TimeoutError as a Retake.

findings.title: No test covers the film's cue list, seek determinism or trace freshness
findings.evidence: No test_*.py references spike, __film or trace.js. The score depends on exactly these 99 cue times, and findings 1 and 2 are seek-order bugs that a forward-vs-reverse seek check catches immediately.
findings.reproduction: grep -ln 'spike\|__film' test_*.py → 'no test references the film or spike_trace'. My probes: 99 cues, 0 differences vs the original; seek-order mismatches only at 81.3–81.9 s and 132.0–133.5 s.
findings.fix: One Playwright pytest: cues equal a golden list; frame(t) after seek(0) equals frame(t) after seek(duration) on a 1/30 s grid; plus an in-memory rerun of spike_trace's scenario compared with trace.js (ignoring uuids and timestamps).

findings.title: 3D frames are cached by count and file name only, so stale frames are reused after the film, textures, scene or engine change
findings.evidence: spike_render: 'if len(list(out.glob("*.jpg"))) < frames:' skips Blender entirely. spike3d.py:362: 'if not chosen and path.exists(): continue'. export() rewrites film.json and textures() re-cuts papers on every run, but nothing ties the frames to film.json, papers/*.png, spike3d.py, SPIKE3D_ENGINE or the Blender version. composite() then lays the NEW world/screen plates and dark values over OLD 3D frames. 0-byte or partially written JPEGs from a killed Blender count as done. The docstring asks for manual deletion, and the running session did exactly that: ps shows 'rm -rf ... clips/spike3d/frames' after editing spike3d.py.
findings.reproduction: spike_render imported with OUT3D pointed at a scratch dir holding 3 zero-byte jpgs, BLENDER='/usr/bin/false' (would fail check=True if run) and a new film.json. Output: 'render3d returned tmp/stale/frames -> Blender never ran; 3 stale frames reused'.
findings.verification: Code read by the lead (spike_render.py:93, spike3d.py skip). This run's frames were invalidated by diffing film.json and the paper textures instead.
findings.fix: Write frames/KEY = sha1(film.json + papers/*.png + spike3d.py + ENGINE). When it differs, delete frames/ before rendering, and drop the count check. Have spike3d render to NNNN.part.jpg and rename it on success.
findings.regrade_reason: a tooling hazard: output is wrong only if the documented manual delete is skipped

findings.title: The REFUSED late 'yes' is staged through a memory call that the app's chat never makes
findings.evidence: conv.answer(stale, True) is called directly on the memory layer. The film (index.html 779–791) shows the customer's 'yes' stamped REFUSED with 'StaleConfirmation: that question is no longer pending'. agent.turn calls conv.answer only for the currently pending proposal (agent.py 257–275), and server.py has no answer endpoint. In the app, a late 'yes' is just a new message.
findings.reproduction: replay_trace.py: 'LATE YES via Agent.turn: trace keys [claims, decisions, extract_error, fallback, rejected, reply_errors] | confirmation: None | reply: 'Here are a couple of ideas.\n\n- **Spicy Chicken Bowl** ($12.00)…' | events 4 -> 4 | classify calls: 0'. By contrast: 'direct conv.answer(stale) -> StaleConfirmation that question is no longer pending'.
findings.fix: Record agent.turn(USER, cid, 'yes') and show its real outcome (no question pending, nothing changed), or caption the beat as a direct memory-API check. Changing the text alone leaves cue times unchanged.

findings.title: data.js is stale against sections.py (S08's second mark is missing), and the next build.py run exits
findings.evidence: data.js S08 marks are [['means this conversation','reply_first','Just this conversation']]. sections.py:55-56 adds ('beside the saved value','ticket_now',...). In the 'tonight' footage the ticket is scrolled out of view (e.g. raw/maya/000517.jpg).
findings.reproduction: build.layout(vos, footage(...)) on current inputs: 'layout SystemExit: S08: 'ticket_now' is not on screen in its footage; check the capture'. With that one mark removed, layout() == data.js sections (True), and footage() == data.js beats (True).
findings.fix: Re-capture 'tonight' with the ticket in view (or drop the mark) and rebuild.

findings.title: The S03 'order ticket' mark lands before the app is on screen and takes its box from a blank frame
findings.evidence: The cue is spoken 2.7 s into the signup footage; the app first appears at 3.772 s. The page clamps the mark to local 3.49 s, where no 'ticket' region exists, then falls back to the first state with one. That state is frame 000000, a pure-white about:blank frame (extrema (255,255)) that build.regions reads as a full-height ticket [1250,-4,1642,1083]. findings.title: The restart wait loop crashes on a non-JSON or error response and has no deadline
findings.evidence: `if httpx.get(...).json()["started_at"] != started: break` with only `except httpx.TransportError: continue`. During a hosted restart a proxy commonly answers 502/503 with an HTML or other body. .json() then raises JSONDecodeError (a ValueError), or ['started_at'] raises KeyError. Both escape the except as a traceback. With no time limit, a restart that never comes hangs forever.
findings.reproduction: `.venv/bin/python -c` with httpx.Response(502, text='<html>...') -> `escapes the except clause: (JSONDecodeError, ValueError, Exception)`; Response(503, json={'detail':...}) -> `escapes: KeyError('started_at')`.
findings.fix: Check `r.status_code == 200` before .json(), and catch (httpx.TransportError, ValueError, KeyError). Add a deadline (e.g. 10 minutes) that records a FAIL and exits.

findings.title: the lockout message and README promise a 15-minute lock, but the window lifts 15 minutes after the oldest of the last five failures
findings.evidence: recent holds the failures inside LOGIN_WINDOW_SECONDS. The sixth attempt is refused with 'Try again in 15 minutes.', but it is allowed as soon as the first of the five ages out. README 305-306: '5 failed attempts per username lock it for 15 minutes'. The guess rate stays at 5 per 15 minutes, so this is a contract and wording issue, not a bypass.
findings.reproduction: r2.py (monotonic patched): failures at t=0,1,2,3,899 s; at t=899.5 -> `429 Too many sign-in attempts for this username. Try again in 15 minutes.`; at t=900.5 -> `401` (the attempt is processed).
findings.fix: Report the real wait, `int(LOGIN_WINDOW_SECONDS - (now - recent[0])) // 60 + 1` minutes, or describe it as a rate ('at most 5 failed sign-ins per 15 minutes') in the message and README.

findings.title: each unauthenticated /api/login costs a 16 MiB scrypt and an in-memory entry per attacker-chosen username, with no cap
findings.evidence: _hash is scrypt with n=2**14 and r=8, which needs 128*r*n = 16 MiB per call. It runs for unknown usernames too (line 98) and releases the GIL, so FastAPI's 40-thread pool can hold about 640 MiB at once. `self._failures[name] = recent + [now]` (94) adds an entry for any name, and the dict is rebuilt in O(n) under the lock on every login (87-88). The README notes 'no per-IP limit' but not this memory exposure, and its Hosting section points at small Render/Fly/Railway instances.
findings.reproduction: Partly measured. Four of this exact scrypt call in threads took 0.059 s against 0.211 s run serially, so the calls do run in parallel (`python -I -c` timing snippet). The ~640 MiB peak is reasoning only (scrypt memory = 128*r*N bytes, times AnyIO's default 40-token thread limiter for sync endpoints); no load test was run, to keep CPU use low.
findings.fix: Bound concurrent hashing with a module-level threading.BoundedSemaphore around _hash, and stop recording failures for usernames that do not exist (or cap len(_failures)).

MAX_MESSAGE counts code points: 2,000 emoji are 8 KB as raw UTF-8 and 24 KB JSON-escaped (Python's json.dumps default, many HTTP clients), which gets 'That request is too large.' although the message is within the documented limit. The page uses JSON.stringify (raw UTF-8) and stays under the cap.
findings.reproduction: r3.py: 2,000 x U+1F600 posted to /api/chat: ensure_ascii=False 8074 bytes -> 200; ensure_ascii=True 24074 bytes -> 413.
findings.fix: Derive the cap from the worst case, `MAX_BODY_BYTES = 12 * MAX_MESSAGE + 1024` (a \uXXXX\uXXXX pair per code point), and correct the comment.

findings.title: a model/provider mismatch or a revoked key reaches customers as 'try again or rephrase' while /api/health says chat is enabled
findings.evidence: EXTRACT_MODEL and REPLY_MODEL are used as given for any provider (85-86). README 59-60 tells users to `export EXTRACT_MODEL=gpt-5.4-mini REPLY_MODEL=gpt-5.4-mini`, and README 66 then says to switch with LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic. Every Anthropic call would then fail with NotFoundError (an APIError), extract() returns an error, and agent.turn answers each message with 200 and _EXTRACT_FAILED ('...Please try again or rephrase your message.'). health reports chat_enabled true (135) because it checks only that the key is set. A revoked key (401) behaves the same way, and only a log warning shows the cause.
findings.reproduction: reasoning: no live call allowed. Path: llm.MODEL_ERRORS catches anthropic.NotFoundError (subclass of APIStatusError, itself an APIError) -> extractor.py:197-199 -> agent.py:252-256.
findings.fix: Treat permanent API errors (AuthenticationError, PermissionDeniedError, NotFoundError) as ModelUnavailable, which gives a 503 with a configuration message, or say in the README that the model pins must change with the provider.

findings.title: rejected sign-ups (invalid PIN, taken username) use up the global registration budget
findings.evidence: `if not sign_ups.allow("all"):` runs before accounts.register validates anything, so every 400 records a hit. 50 malformed requests (no scrypt, no DB write, free to send) block all new sign-ups for an hour, and honest typos count too.
findings.reproduction: r2.py with REGISTRATIONS=(3,3600): three {'username':'x','pin':'1'} -> [400, 400, 400]; then a valid sign-up -> `429 {'detail': 'Too many new accounts right now. Try again in an hour.'}`.
findings.fix: Run the cheap USERNAME/PIN format checks before sign_ups.allow, so only well-formed requests are counted.

findings.title: server and account behaviors with no test
findings.evidence: Two mutants survive. In one, /api/me always returns question=None, although the page restores a waiting question from it after a reload (index.html:312-314). In the other, Accounts.login no longer clears failures after a successful sign-in. Also untested: chat_enabled true with an injected client, sliding-window expiry in _Window, and the '' handling of EXTRACT_MODEL/REPLY_MODEL.
findings.reproduction: mutate.py -> 'me-drops-question SURVIVED (79 passed)', 'login-success-keeps-failures SURVIVED (79 passed)'.
findings.fix: Over HTTP, after 'I'm no longer allergic to peanuts.', assert that GET /api/me?conversation_id=cid returns that question. In test_login_attempts, after 4 failures and a success, one more failure must give 401, not 429.

findings.title: chat rate limits are charged for requests that never reach the model
findings.evidence: per_user.allow and total.allow (191-194) run before agent.turn, which raises UnknownConversation (404) or ModelUnavailable (503) before any model call. A per-user hit is also recorded when total.allow then refuses. On a 404 the page (index.html:368-372) asks the user to resend, so a conversation that ended while idle costs two hits per message.
findings.reproduction: r2.py with CHAT_PER_USER=(3,600): three chats to 'deadbeef-0000' -> [404, 404, 404]; then a chat to the real conversation -> `429 {'detail': "You're sending messages quickly. Wait a few minutes, then try again."}`.
findings.fix: Do the 404 and 503 checks before the limiters (look up the conversation and the client first), and check total before recording the per-user hit.

findings.title: `.main { height: calc(100% - 64px) }` assumes a 64px header; the real header is 67px, or 122px when it wraps
findings.evidence: Magic 64px. The header is padding 14px x 2, a 26px brand and 38px link buttons, plus a border. It wraps (flex-wrap) at desktop widths near the 861px breakpoint, for example with a long username.
findings.reproduction: Playwright scratch/audit/ui_checks.py scenario D. `1280x800: header 67.34, docScroll 803, inner 800, composerBottom 803.3` (the page always scrolls 3px). `900x800 username=32 chars: header 121.69, docScroll 858, inner 800` (58px of overflow; the composer is pushed below the fold until the page scrolls).
findings.fix: Make #app a flex column (header auto, .main flex:1; min-height:0) and drop the calc.

findings.title: Dead CSS rule .msg.note

findings.title: api() treats `detail` as a string; FastAPI's 422 detail is a list, so the user sees '[object Object]'
findings.evidence: `new Error(data.detail || `Request failed (${res.status})`)`. For a 422 (e.g. conversation_id null, which the two paths above produce), data.detail is an array of objects, and Error() stringifies it to '[object Object]'.
findings.reproduction: Same runs as above: `problem shown after sending: '[object Object]'`.
findings.fix: `const msg = typeof data.detail === "string" ? data.detail : `Request failed (${res.status})`;`

findings.title: The trace says the model's reply 'failed checks' when the model was in fact unreachable
findings.evidence: `if (t.fallback) lines.push("Reply built from menu data only (the model's reply failed checks)")`. agent._reply sets trace.fallback = True after MODEL_ERRORS too (agent.py 352-355, 377). test_narration_outage_falls_back_to_grounded_dishes asserts fallback for an API outage.
findings.reproduction: reasoning: agent.py breaks out on MODEL_ERRORS and then sets trace['fallback']=True; PUBLIC_TRACE forwards 'fallback'; the UI has only the one 'failed checks' wording.
findings.fix: Word it 'Reply built from menu data only (the model's reply was unavailable or broke the rules)'.

findings.title: Recovery from an ended conversation swallows its own failure, then says 'I started one'
findings.evidence:
`await startConversation(true).catch(() => {}); add("problem", `

${esc(err.message)} I started one; please send your message again.

`);`. If creating the conversation fails, conversationId is left null (startConversation sets it to null first), and the next send fails with a 422.
findings.reproduction: Playwright scratch/audit/ui_checks.py scenario F: /api/chat returns 404 and /api/conversations returns 500. Output: `problem shown: 'This conversation has ended. Start a new one. I started one; please send your message again.'` / `conversationId now: None` / `next send: '[object Object]'`.
findings.fix:
try { await startConversation(true); add(...'I started one'...) } catch (e2) { if (e2.status === 401) showAuth(); else add("problem", `

${esc(e2.message)}

`); }

findings.title: Enter that commits an IME composition (Japanese, Chinese, Korean input) sends the half-typed message
findings.evidence: `if (e.key === "Enter" && !e.shiftKey) { e.preventDefault(); $("composer").requestSubmit(); }` has no `e.isComposing` / keyCode 229 guard. Browsers that report the commit Enter as key 'Enter' with isComposing=true (MDN's documented case) will submit.
findings.reproduction: Playwright scratch/audit/ui_checks2.py dispatches a synthetic keydown {key:'Enter', keyCode:229, isComposing:true} to the textarea: `user messages before/after: 0 1 | textarea now: ''`. A synthetic event shows that the handler ignores isComposing. Behavior with a real IME was not tested.
findings.fix: `if (e.isComposing || e.keyCode === 229) return;` at the top of the keydown handler.

findings.title: The ticket toggle's label and aria-expanded are wrong after the window narrows from desktop to phone width
findings.evidence: On desktop the load code removes 'collapsed' (line 427) but leaves the button at 'Show what I remember' / aria-expanded=false. Below 861px the ticket is visible while the button says Show. The first click hides it and the label does not change.
findings.reproduction: Playwright scratch/audit/ui_checks2.py: load at 1280px, then resize to 700px. Output: `after resize: ticket visible, label, aria-expanded = (True, 'Show what I remember', 'false')` / `after 1st click: (False, 'Show what I remember', 'false')`.
findings.fix: Set the label and aria-expanded from the actual state when collapsed is removed on load (or derive them in the click handler from the visibility before the toggle).

findings.title: A failed menu request is silent: the dialog never opens and the rejection is unhandled
findings.evidence: `const m = await api("/api/menu");` in a click handler, with no try/catch.
findings.reproduction: Playwright scratch/audit/ui_checks.py scenario G: /api/menu returns 500. Output: `dialog open: False | visible error in page: [] | uncaught: ['Something went wrong.']`.

Wrap it in try/catch and add("problem", `

${esc(err.message)}

`) on failure.

findings.title: Prompt-hygiene test skips the yes/no classifier prompt, which contains confirmation eval case c18's reply verbatim
findings.evidence: test_prompt_contains_no_eval_utterances checks only extractor_cases against EXTRACT_SYSTEM. extractor.REPLY_SYSTEM line 225 lists hedges ("I guess", "probably"), and confirmation_cases c18 is reply 'probably' -> expected 'unclear'. That case counts in the README's 'Yes/no classifier accuracy 18/18'.

findings.title: Some rule outcomes run only inside the P6 sweep, which asserts only that nothing loosens
findings.evidence: SPEC §11 claims unit coverage of 'decide rules R1–R11'. R4 (an aspiration on an allergen, or an aspiration negating a diet) never has its outcome asserted, nor does the R9 'hedged restatement' apply-only branch (memory.py:346-347). A regression from R4 to R8, or from R9 apply to apply+confirm, would pass.

findings.note: File is read-only (chmod 444) by the owner's choice; any fix is the owner's decision.

findings.title: serve() trusts any process already listening on port 8790
findings.evidence: The health loop accepts a 200 from any process and never checks srv.poll(). If a stale server holds the port (e.g. a crashed --preview run), the new uvicorn exits silently (stdout and stderr go to DEVNULL) and the session films the stale server. It fails late, at the sqlite read of the new capture.db ('no such table: users'), after tokens are spent.
findings.reproduction: reasoning: lines 287-299
findings.fix: Check `srv.poll() is None` in the loop and abort if the port is already bound before starting the server.

findings.title: Capture provenance is incomplete: model, attempt number, and the scripted-server menu refilm are not recorded
findings.evidence: serve() inherits EXTRACT_MODEL/REPLY_MODEL/LLM_PROVIDER from the shell, but DATA does not record the model the README says was filmed (gpt-5.4-mini), nor the attempt that passed. menu_only() refilms menu_note on preview.py (FakeLLM) and updates only beats.json; capture_data.json still says preview False and holds the old note 'ok   menu_note: allergen note shown' (current check text: 'allergen note in view'). beats.json menu_note.session == 'menu', so the current film uses the refilm. build.py's storyboard says 'Captures are the real app on the live model'.

findings.title: Blender exits 0 when spike3d.py raises a Python exception
findings.evidence: subprocess.run([BLENDER, '--background', '--python', ..., '--', ...], check=True) has no '--python-exit-code'. Its default is 0, which disables it. A KeyError in place() at frame N therefore 'succeeds'. composite then fails on the first missing frame with a FileNotFoundError that hides the traceback, or, with old frames on disk (F4), does not fail at all.

findings.fix_applied: Blender runs with --python-exit-code 1.

findings.title: the timeline is built before fonts load, so wire geometry differs between cold and warm renders (by 1.5 px / 3 px)
findings.evidence: Lines 170-711 build the whole timeline while the script is parsed. SCENES.grounding (line 531) measures tok.offsetLeft/offsetWidth/offsetTop to anchor the wires. Fonts are awaited only at lines 723-724, just before __film is exposed, and they come from Google Fonts (line 6). So the result depends on whether the font was already cached.
findings.reproduction: probe_walk.py loads the page twice in one browser context. First load (cold): wire starts built at ['M496.5,384','M642.5,384'], while the post-load layout puts the tokens at ['M495,381','M641,381']. Second load (cached): built at ['M496,381','M642,381']. Same input, different output between renders. The magnitude is small, but it is real non-determinism.
findings.fix: Wrap the timeline construction in the fonts-ready promise (await document.fonts.load(...) first), and embed the fonts as data: URIs the way spike/index.html does.
findings.regrade_reason: the effect is a 1.5-3 px wire offset between cold and warm loads, invisible at film scale
findings.fix_applied: The page loads its fonts before building the timeline (async start). Wire geometry is identical on cold and warm loads.

findings.title: A reply in flight can recommend a newly saved allergen because it validates against a stale profile
findings.evidence: agent.py:284-286: with self._lock: / profile, pending = conv.profile(), conv.pending / recs = recommend(self.menu, profile.active). agent.py:295-296: message, picks = self._reply(state, text, profile, recs, changes, notice, trace) / reply, mentioned = render(message, picks, self.menu, recs, profile.active["budget_max"]). agent.py:306: return TurnResult(reply, mentioned, changes, question, profile_view(profile), trace).
findings.failure: A second conversation can save a durable peanut allergy while the first reply model call is pending. The first request subsequently validates and renders its picks with its earlier eligible set, returning Chicken Satay with no warning and a stale empty profile. Memory remains correctly saved; the returned recommendation is unsafe relative to the already committed allergy.
findings.reproduction: Create one Agent with EventStore(":memory:") and the shipped menu, two conversations for user u, and FakeLLM. Block the first responder with threading.Event after it receives its briefing; its output is {"message":"Try this.","recommend":["S4"]}. While blocked, run a turn in the second conversation extracting current/asserted allergen peanut. Wait for this turn to finish; then release the first responder. Observed current_allergens=["peanut"], returned=[{"id":"S4","name":"Chicken Satay","price":9.0,"kind":"rec","warnings":[]}]. Reproduced before and after the MM-005 fix without any network or persistent database.
findings.verification: Independent in-memory threaded reproduction against agent.py SHA256 ad1b6288cc5325f83ebe95ebe6dc471764b00b51020bfc42e6c4cdb82ea64450. Full current test suite: 196 passed in 1.74s. Existing tests do not catch this interleaving.
findings.falsification: Read the memory lock, recommend(), _reply()/check_reply(), render(), and HTTP chat caller. The lock serializes memory changes but is released before the model call. The later lock only updates history; no current profile or event sequence is checked before returning. The normal UI busy flag only covers one page; two conversations/tabs can issue this interleaving. This is a single-process failure, not the documented multi-process limitation.
findings.fix: Bind the response to an event-log version. Recheck the version and current profile after the model returns, revalidate or discard stale picks and regenerate any stale prose/profile, and make the validation/publication decision atomic relative to memory writes. Add a controlled two-conversation regression test.
